glossary.Asymmetrical: Affecting the two sides of the body unequally, for example one knee but not the other.
glossary.Extra-articular: Features occurring outside the joints, such as eye, skin or tendon involvement.
glossary.Genitourinary (GU): Relating to the genital and urinary organs.
glossary.Gastrointestinal (GI): Relating to the stomach and intestines.
glossary.Post-enteric: Following a bowel infection, typically one causing diarrhoea.
glossary.Gram-negative: Bacteria that stain pink on Gram stain because of a thin cell wall and outer membrane.
glossary.Diplococci: Round bacteria that sit in pairs, such as Neisseria.
glossary.Intracellular: Located inside cells, for example bacteria seen inside neutrophils.
glossary.Triad: A group of three features that together suggest a diagnosis.
glossary.Maculopapular: A rash with both flat (macules) and raised (papules) spots.
glossary.Vesicle: A small fluid-filled blister under 5 mm across.
glossary.Sausage digit: A finger or toe swollen along its whole length, the lay term for dactylitis.
glossary.Tendonitis: Inflammation of a tendon, causing pain on movement.
glossary.Ankylosing spondylitis: Chronic HLA-B27-linked inflammatory arthritis of the spine and sacroiliac joints that can fuse the vertebrae.
glossary.Chronic arthritis: Joint inflammation persisting beyond about six months.
glossary.STI screen: Tests for sexually transmitted infections, usually urine or swab NAAT for chlamydia and gonorrhoea.
glossary.Stool culture: Growing bacteria from a faeces sample to identify a gut infection.
glossary.Culture negative: No organism grows when the sample is cultured in the laboratory.
glossary.Crystals: Urate or calcium pyrophosphate crystals in joint fluid, which point to gout or pseudogout.
glossary.White cell count (WCC): The number of white blood cells in a sample; high counts suggest inflammation or infection.
glossary.Ibuprofen: A common oral NSAID used for pain and inflammation.
glossary.Naproxen: A longer-acting oral NSAID used for inflammatory joint pain.
glossary.Corticosteroid: Anti-inflammatory steroid drug, such as prednisolone or methylprednisolone.
glossary.Rheumatology: The medical specialty that manages joint, muscle and autoimmune inflammatory diseases.
glossary.Systemic symptoms: Whole-body features such as fever, sweats and malaise.
glossary.Antigen: A molecule that the immune system recognises and responds to.
glossary.Self-peptide: A small fragment of the body's own protein displayed to immune cells.
glossary.Autoimmune: When the immune system attacks the body's own tissues.
glossary.Immune-mediated: Damage caused by the body's immune response rather than directly by a microbe.
glossary.Plantar fascia: The thick band of tissue running along the sole from the heel to the toes.
